summary.headline: Sejal Glass Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR117.95 crore, up 52.88% YoY; management guides FY27 revenue growth of minimum 25%, up to 40%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 52.88% YoY to INR117.95 crore, with India up 67.03% to INR36.43 crore and UAE up 47.31% to INR81.52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA grew over 44% YoY to INR18 crore and PAT grew over 63% YoY to INR7.22 crore. Management cited a one-time-like INR1 crore people-cost hit from appraisals and a Taloja labour union agreement, plus UAE logistics and fuel-related cost increases, as drags on Q1 margin. Guidance was framed as a 25% minimum and up to 40% revenue growth for FY27, with EBITDA margin up about 1% and PAT margin of 9-10% targeted, mainly from Q3-Q4.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR52 crore total, of which term loan ~INR38 crore and working capital ~INR14 crore

segments.name: India (Silvassa, Taloja, Erode)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR36.43 crore, up 67.03% YoY; India exports about 6% of sales, domestic 94%. Silvassa utilisation ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Revenue INR81.52 crore, up 47.31% YoY; utilisation ~71% on tempering base line, with 95% of UAE output sold locally and in GCC, Africa emerging. Order book about AED70-72 million.

segments.name: Railway / fire-safety / bulletproof verticals
segments.commentary: Railway was under 1% of Q1 revenue; fire-rated glass production to start Q3 FY27. Management targets 10% of revenue from these verticals next year, including railway.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at minimum 25%, with upside to around 40% if geopolitical situation stabilises and order inflows continue.
FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by about 1% over upcoming quarters; PAT margin target of around 9% (CFO) to 9-10% (promoter) for FY27, mainly in Q3 and Q4.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected at INR140-145 crore (15-20% QoQ growth from Q1 INR118 crore).
FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25% YoY (early-stage guidance).
UAE monthly revenue on track to AED31 million in Q1 and AED35 million in Q2 per prior commentary; July at AED11.87 million.
Management indicated 25-40% annual growth range over the next 3-4 years.
Expected UAE revenue mix shift to around 60:40 (UAE:India) this year and 50:50 next year.
capex_capacity: UAE third tempering line (capex incl. fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million) installed; commercial production expected Q3 FY27 end, third line utilisation 15-20% initially. UAE total tempering capacity to ~24 lakh sq m per annum.
UAE plant utilisation ~71% now, target 85%; existing two lines expected to reach ~75%.
Silvassa targeted at 85-90% by year end; Taloja 75% in coming quarters; Erode 25-30% in coming quarters.
India capex is maintenance-type, below INR1 crore per item.
Funding: UAE capex from internal accruals plus proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan, roughly 50:50 debt-equity.

Management indicated capacity additions across UAE third line and Taloja/Erode could add about INR75 crore revenue capacity on top of ~INR600 crore from existing capacity (analyst-stated, confirmed by promoter).
demand_pricing: UAE order book about AED70-72 million (~INR175 crore), up from ~AED50 million; incremental inflow AED22-27 million; execution from June-July over next two quarters.
India order inflow above INR50 crore from developers including Godrej, L&T, Prestige and Raheja, to be executed over about 6 months.
Customer execution is gated by end-customer site readiness and design approvals, delaying size release; management says July UAE revenue already crossed AED11.87 million.
Bad debts below 0.5% over last three years; top 15 clients currently >70% of India business, ~200 repeat clients.
Management says no listed architectural glass peer in India; Asahi India Glass is mainly automotive and Borosil is solar.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin guidance and what is the closing order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated EBITDA up about 1% and PAT around 9%; order book referenced as India >INR50 crore and UAE ~AED70 million. Promoter said 25% is minimum growth, up to 40% upside, after an earlier TV comment of 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Current and peak capacity utilisation by plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Silvassa ~77%, Taloja ~55%, Erode ~15%, UAE ~71%. Targets: Silvassa 85-90% by year end, Taloja 75%, Erode 25-30%, UAE 85%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there capex planned and how much capacity will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: India capex under INR1 crore per item for maintenance. UAE third tempering line and fire-rated tech total ~AED15 million; commercial production Q3 end; total tempering capacity ~24 lakh sq m per annum.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the Q1 margin squeeze?
qa_highlights.answer: Appraisal and yearly increments plus a Taloja labour union agreement added about INR1 crore people cost; UAE logistics hit by June war disruption; raw material costs up about 1% due to diesel and energy surcharge.

qa_highlights.question: Why has UAE monthly sales stayed near AED10-10.5 million despite a AED60-70 million order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Tailor-made orders are released in size only when end customers are ready, so production timing lags order inflow. July UAE revenue reached AED11.87 million.

qa_highlights.question: How is the UAE capex funded and what are FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded from internal accruals plus a proposed ~AED7 million long-term bank loan. FY28 revenue growth expected at least 25%, too early for margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Railway and new vertical contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway under 1% of Q1 revenue; target 10% of revenue from railway, fire-safety and related verticals next year. Approved vendor for Kapurthala, Raebareli and Chennai railway facilities.
